items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (durabilityManager, processNotifySubsLocked), but doc comments are one-liners. Non-obvious logic has no explanation: `endSeqNum := info.SeqNum + base.SeqNum(info.KeyCount)`. Step comments like `// 1. Fire EventListener callback` add little. New Batch fields `commitJobID int` look unaligned.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Tracking is split out into durability.go (480 lines), which is good. But commit.go builds the same BatchDurableInfo literal 4 times (prepare error, apply error, sync, goroutine). WaitForDurability is about 60 lines and repeats the firstErr/closedErr precedence checks inline.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Errors are propagated and close unblocks waiters. Off-by-one: highest durable = SeqNum+KeyCount, one past the batch's last seqnum, so a later seqnum can report durable early. A goroutine per NoSyncWait commit reads b.commitErr on a batch that may be reused. Waiter subs are uncapped. 4 hidden tests fail.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: applyInternal calls `d.newJobID()` on every sync commit, even with no BatchDurable configured. This shifts JobIDs in existing flush/compaction events (testdata/event_listener rewritten from [JOB 2] to [JOB 3] and so on). It also adds a per-commit registerJob mutex, and NoSyncWait sync commits now spawn a goroutine each.
